analysis.title: Marketcolour + Memory / Earnings (Ioannis Blekos, 12 Nov 2026)
key_insights: US equities closed higher on 11 Nov while the bond market was closed for Veterans Day: SPX +131bps to 7619 (9 of 11 sectors up, Tech +390bps, Energy +205bps, Discretionary -23bps), NDX +160bps to 25466, DJIA +49bps to 52486, VIX -10% to 17.48.
NDX is back above its 200-dma and pre-election levels. Semis are up nearly 20% from the local lows, attributed to cleaner positioning, vol resetting lower and election narratives being digested.
Retail engagement was high: GS Retail Favorite basket +495bps, its third best day in three years.
Nvidia closed with a 14-day RSI of about 24, the lowest since mid-2019, when NVDA was a roughly $100bn market cap stock.

Memory debate (MU, SNDK, HDDs), credited to Peter Callahan. Bull points: 2-4x forward P/E approaching tangible book value, capital return programs just starting (focus on MU earnings), firm or rising spot prices especially DRAM, and guided favorable supply/demand through 2027+.

Memory bear points: the market worries about over-earning given the size of ASP tailwinds early in the cycle, particularly if the build cycle becomes less linear. Supply from new or emerging entrants is still to be determined. Low P/E multiples in cycles are as much a bear case as a bull case.
Hedge fund performance: systematic long/short managers +1.25% (a +2.6 SD move, about 3/4 of funds up), the best day since June. Fundamental +0.4% (+1.3% MTD), multi-strats +0.7% (+0.2% MTD).

Data center ballot measures: 41 were voted on and the pro-restriction side won nearly all. Half were in Ohio, and Maine, Illinois and Kansas accounted for nearly all the rest, all at town level. Voters hold a clear opinion when asked but give the issue little thought otherwise.

An NY Times poll taken just before the election shows the public is not focused on data centers when asked to name the most important issue for their vote, despite Texas and Ohio being at the center of the political debate.
Europe: EU Semis (GSSBSEMI) +5.6%, Electricals (GSXEACDC) +2.9% and on course for their best week since June, Defense (GSSBDEFE) -2.5% and under pressure again.

Siemens Q4: small beat and guide ahead, with Digital Industries (DI) the focus. Group orders +58% were a large beat mainly from Mobility. DI orders +15% vs consensus +2%, Smart Infrastructure (SI) orders +39% vs consensus +23%. Organic growth +10% vs consensus +8.5%. Adj. EBITA was a 2% beat, with SI helped by tariff refunds.

Siemens margins beat in all core divisions: DI 20.9% vs consensus 18.9%, SI 20.3% vs 19.5%, Mobility 9.5% vs 8.7%. Guidance is +9-11% group growth (consensus 8.5%), DI +8-12% (consensus +8%), SI +11-13% (consensus 11%). Positioning was light.

Siemens Energy (Buy, PT EUR200, 50% upside): new guidance is a 7% upgrade to Visible Alpha consensus profit before special items at the midpoint, 16% at the top end. It implies a 6x rise in profit margin before special items by FY2030 vs FY2025 and leaves the stock at 4-5x 2030 EV/EBITDA.

PGHN and TKO moved to Sell. PGHN faces downside risk to gross inflows and recurring fee economics. TKO's strong relative share price contrasts with weaker near-term fundraising, expected to stay subdued through 2027 and early 2028, with roll-off of PE catch-up fees a further headwind to FRE margin.

Allianz 3Q26 (Buy, PT EUR465): group operating profit a 10% beat vs company-collected consensus, from a 4% P&C beat (higher investment income), an 18% asset management beat and lower corporate costs. Combined ratio and insurance revenue were in line. Attritional loss ratio is about 80bps worse than consensus, with weather and large losses about 90bps above normal.

Zurich 3Q26: P&C GWP growth 4% and insurance revenue growth 7%. GWP was broadly in line with GS expectations and insurance revenue about 2% higher. Implied underlying GWP growth of 7% vs GS estimate 4.5%, from better price (1.0% vs -0.2%) and volume (6% vs 4.7%). EMEA was strongest, North America weaker (+0.1% vs 3%) on lower implied volume.

Munich Re: the bottom line and new guidance were already known, so focus is on details. Bears will highlight the P&C Re undiscounted normalized COR miss of 1.8ppts, with consensus looking too high for next year. GS sees the stock down 1-2%.

Rolls-Royce trading statement in line. EFH run-rating toward the lower end of guidance, financial guidance unchanged, mid-term targets to be revisited in February. New interim buyback of GBP1.5bn to complete by FY27 results, as the previous GBP2.5bn is nearly done, taking total buybacks to GBP4bn by end-February against an original GBP7-9bn commitment by 2028. Indicated +1%.

PGHN (Partners Group): downside risk to gross inflows and recurring fee economics.
Fundraising expected to stay subdued through 2027 and early 2028, and roll-off of private equity catch-up fees is a further headwind to FRE margin.
Allianz 3Q26 first take: group operating profit a 10% beat vs company-collected consensus, led by P&C and asset management.
Memory stocks trade at 2-4x forward P/E near tangible book value and are starting capital return programs, with attention on MU earnings.
Grouped with MU in the memory debate, with cheap valuation and firm spot prices set against over-earning concerns.

sector_views.rationale: Cheap valuations, rising DRAM spot prices and guided favorable supply/demand through 2027+ are balanced by worries about peak earnings, new supply entrants and low-P/E multiples signaling a cycle top.
GSSBSEMI +5.6% extending its rally. This is price action in the note, not an explicit bank view.
GSSBDEFE -2.5% and under pressure again. This is price action, not an explicit view.

Siemens Energy: new guidance is a 7% upgrade to Visible Alpha consensus profit before special items at the midpoint and 16% at the top end.

Allianz 3Q26 (reported): group operating profit a 10% beat vs company-collected consensus, with P&C +4%, asset management +18% and lower corporate costs. Current-year attritional undiscounted loss ratio about 80bps worse than consensus.
Zurich 3Q26 (reported): P&C GWP +4% y/y and insurance revenue +7%. There is no company-collected consensus for 3Q. Implied underlying GWP growth of 7% vs GS estimate 4.5%.
